text:
noah li: opened a small docs PR to add a Rust example for Optimize Toolkit (kv prefetch + batching + quant profiles). current docs only show Go/JS and people asked for Rust. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/588

dina park: great—i can draft the Rust snippet. do we want an async example or sync? most Rust users will prefer async with tokio.

noah li: async tokio please. keep it tiny, show ContinuousBatcher equivalent and how to set the shortseq quant profile.

rob k.: CI note: the old draft referenced an external crate example that wasn't vendored; replace with internal example path /examples/optimize/rust/kv_prefetch.rs so docs extraction works.

dina park: ack. i'll use internal path and add a tiny benchmark command. also include a short fallback sentence when kv prefetch misses.

ux-erin: UX request: please add a concise callout box: "Optional: KV prefetch improves throughput for short, repeated prompts. Not required." Keep language friendly to newcomers.

dina park: drafting snippet now. proposed minimal Rust snippet:
```rust
let client = redwood::Client::new(std::env::var("REDWOOD_API_KEY").unwrap());
let batcher = optimize::ContinuousBatcher::new(client).with_kv_prefetch();
let resp = batcher.generate("Summarize: ...").with_quant_profile("shortseq").await?;
println!("{}", resp.text);
```

noah li: looks good. can you add the microbench command: `cargo run --example kv_prefetch -- --profile shortseq --batch continuous`
dina park: added microbench line and a 2-row mini table (legacy vs prefetch+continuous) showing tokens/sec and p95 latency. included UX callout box and the fallback note: "On cache miss, requests use the single-path request; expect ~1.7-1.9x p95."

rob k.: left a small PR comment suggesting we link to Dedicated docs for pinning quant profiles: /dedicated/configure-quant-profiles. also fixed the internal example path.
